subject: Staggered scale path and SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Evan Cooper <evan@aperturehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aperturehealth.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity uplift inquiry — short timeline

Hi Marissa,

We’re seeing a sharp increase in production traffic for our summarization service (legal ingest pipeline) and expect to need a material capacity bump ahead of our renewal. Current commit is 32 GPUs (A100-eq). Can you outline what a mid-term top-up would look like for an incremental ~40 GPUs for the next 6–9 months?

Tightly scoped asks:
- Price per committed GPU (monthly) for a mid-term top-up vs adding to renewal
- Any required term extension or minimums
- Throughput SLOs we can expect if we scale to ~70 GPUs total (token/sec estimates welcome)
- Whether we can structure staged increases (we’d prefer a staircase approach over a single step)
- Any credits for a short POC of the larger pool (we want to validate tail-latency at scale)

Attached: aperture_current_usage_report.csv (deltas for last 90 days).

Would prefer a call this week if possible — Evan

--
Evan Cooper
Head of Platform Engineering, Aperture Health
evan@aperturehealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cooper <evan@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift inquiry — short timeline

Thanks for the details, Evan — we can do this and I outlined three pragmatic paths below. Quick note that I looped in pricing and solutions to validate numbers and SLO language.

High-level options (summary):
1) Short-term top-up (3–9 months) — add 40 GPUs as a committed top-up. Monthly commit increases from 32 -> 72 GPUs. Pricing: mid-term uplift rate (one-time uplift factor) + standard reserved rate. No mandatory term extension if you keep original renewal date, but step-up discount is smaller.

2) Staggered/staircase scale (recommended) — a 6–12 month phased ramp: +20 GPUs now, +20 GPUs at month-3 (or when hit utilization trigger). Lower blended discount vs immediate top-up but better budgeting. Can include one-time eval credit.

3) Renewal reprofile (if you want this permanent) — fold new baseline into renewal with a blended rate and longer term (12–24 months) to get deeper discounts and guaranteed throughput SLO.

SLA tradeoffs: you can get tighter latency SLOs (99.9% per-window) with a higher committed baseline and pre-warm buffer; if you accept 99.5% SLO we can lower price ~6–8% and allow more elastic spill to burst.

Next steps: I attached a preliminary estimate (prelim-topup-estimate.csv) and a quick pricing visual (staircase_pricing_v1.pdf). Can we schedule 30m today or tomorrow to walk numbers? If helpful I can include a factual SLO snippet for legal review.

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: staircase_pricing_v1.pdf (pdf), prelim-topup-estimate.csv (csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 14:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: Capacity uplift inquiry — pricing guidance needed

Marissa — rough numbers and structure below. I kept it flexible so we can convert to formal quote once they pick a path.

Assumptions: current baseline 32 GPUs; target incremental 40 GPUs (72 total). Pricing shown as blended monthly committed price per GPU (USD, illustrative):
- Option A (short top-up, 6 months): $5,400 / GPU-mo (mid-term uplift + reserved baseline) => est. monthly commit ~$388,800
- Option B (staggered 6-month staircase, 20/20): month 0–2: +20 GPUs at $5,000/GPU-mo; month 3–6: +20 GPUs at $4,700/GPU-mo (blended if onboarded) => est. blended monthly ~$345k once fully on
- Option C (renewal reprofile, 12–24 mo): $4,200 / GPU-mo blended for new baseline if they fold into renewal and extend term => deeper discount but requires term alignment

SLO note (for legal): "Redwood will configure a dedicated GPU pool sized per the agreed commit. For the committed baseline, Redwood provides a Latency SLO of 99.9%/billing window for p95 tail-latency on <model-family> under normal workload patterns. For staged or burst capacity, Redwood guarantees best-effort throughput with defined pre-warm windows; full 99.9% latency SLO applies to committed baseline only."

Credits: we can offer either a $25k credit against the first invoice of the top-up or 2 weeks of burst capacity (no commit accounting) as a validation window. Both are okay but credit is cleaner for accounting.

No step-down fees within a 60-day cooling window if they reduce staged increases prior to the second step — after that we require a 90-day notice for renegotiation or apply a minimal usage shortfall fee (standard practice).

I suggest we present these three options to Evan and push for Option B as it balances cost vs risk.

-Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Proposal: three paths for Aperture mid-term scale (options A/B/C)

Evan — thanks again. Per our call this morning I’m attaching a concise proposal with three packaged options (pdf). Summary:

- Option A — Short top-up (6 months): immediate +40 GPUs as committed top-up. Fastest path, modest discount.
- Option B — Staggered scale (recommended): +20 GPUs now, +20 GPUs at month-3 conditional on utilization trigger or mutual sign-off. Lower blended price, includes $25k POC credit you can apply to first invoice. Cooling window: 60 days for step cancellation with no penalty.
- Option C — Renewal reprofile (12–24 months): incorporate new baseline at renewal to secure best-in-class discount and a 99.9% committed latency SLO.

I attached the proposal (Aperture_topup_proposal_v3.pdf) and included a DocuSign link for Option B (if you want to accept in principle and send to procurement). The DocuSign contains the pricing sheet only; legal T&Cs follow our standard amendment flow.

Requested decision date: May 12, 2027 to allow capacity planning before June ramp. If you want, we can also provision a small pre-warm buffer the week before go-live (charged at standard burst rate unless the $25k credit applies).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/templates/ABC123-topup-Aperture

Best,
Marissa
